content.text: I'm judging this as a standard two-part FRQ-style item. Part (a) is a loop with % 10 and / 10 (3 points). Part (b) is a while loop that calls digitSum and tests divisibility with %, starting from start (4 points). The concepts are standard for Unit 2, with a moderate number of reasoning steps. There is no heavy arithmetic or reading, and the preconditions are clearly stated (n >= 0, start >= 1), so a digit sum of 0 never causes a divide-by-zero in part (b). The main subtlety is the loop boundary, which must include start itself, and the item also tests whether the student reuses digitSum. This matches a typical exam-style FRQ.
